claims.text: Nanometer-scale regions with chemical short-range order occur in multi-component concentrated alloys.
Chemical short-range order produces spatial fluctuations in local shear-fault or generalized planar-fault energy.
Local fault-energy fluctuations create dislocation pinning or detrapping barriers.
The resulting increase in lattice friction is a governing origin of elevated strength in metastable concentrated alloys.
CrCoNi can be treated as a metastable single-phase concentrated alloy in the proposed initial condition.
The homogenized CrCoNi sample is predominantly characterized by L11-type short-range order.
Heat treatment promotes L12-type short-range order within nanoclusters in CrCoNi.
The heat-treated and homogenized samples can be compared at identical composition and otherwise identical overall microstructure, differing only in short-range order.
L12-type ordered nanoclusters specifically have locally enhanced shear-fault energy relative to the homogenized L11-dominated state.
Short-range ordering alters dislocation-slip behavior in CrCoNi.
Fault-energy fluctuations and local chemical order can produce roughened or wavy dislocation pathways.
Promoting L12-type order by heat treatment will increase yield strength relative to the homogenized L11-dominated baseline.
The heat-treated sample will exhibit more pronounced dislocation pinning and more restricted slip-system activation than the baseline.
The proposed behavior should hold at room or moderately low temperature while the alloy retains its metastable phase.
Extremely high temperatures can disorder concentrated solid solutions and thereby remove the proposed ordering-dependent behavior.
Electron nanodiffraction and atom probe tomography can characterize the targeted local chemical ordering in CrCoNi.
High-resolution diffraction can directly verify the associated local shear-fault-energy fluctuations.
The quantitative contribution of fault-energy fluctuations relative to solid-solution and forest-dislocation hardening may vary with composition and processing.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis frames the comparator as a homogeneous random solid solution, whereas the specified baseline is predominantly L11 ordered; the initial-state field ambiguously allows either random or L11 order. Thus the actual reference state for the claimed strengthening effect is inconsistent.
